title: Benchmarks
description: Sizes are written height x width everywhere (375x1242, as in fastforks bench --size).
html:
kernels (our CUDA kernels) against portable (plain PyTorch, each model's tested precision) and the original authors' code. One RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 12.8 kernels (13.0 for four stereo families), cuDNN 9.24. Stereo and depth rows use real images (KITTI 2015 000000_10, Middlebury Motorcycle) as uint8 CUDA tensors with default options; other tasks use a synthetic input at the task's default size. Speeds are medians of warm runs (5 for most rows; each row's protocol is in docs/data/speed.jsonl); peak memory is torch's peak allocated / reserved GPU MiB (CUDA, weights included) over the first and the timed calls. fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW measures your GPU (it uses 10 runs).

Sizes are written height x width everywhere (375x1242, as in fastforks bench --size).

To choose a model, use the overview: one standard size per task, generated from the same data. The tables below give one table per task and scene (each model at the standard size, or its own input where it has no other; the model pages list every measured size), the startup times and, at the end, the same models at fixed sizes up to 12 MP.

Accuracy matches the original code. On ETH3D and Middlebury (the "Measured" tables on the model pages) both modes stay within 0.15 bad-% / 0.025 EPE of the original with the same checkpoint for AANet, AANet+, CoEx, IGEV, Selective-IGEV, LiteAnyStereo V2 M/H, DEFOM, FoundationStereo-L and CREStereo. S2M2 is better (up to 1 bad-% lower) because our port uses the cost-volume lookup convention the released weights were trained with.

The accuracy columns on the model pages check parity (original code vs portable vs kernels) on public images; they are not a ranking. Variants trained or fine-tuned on ETH3D / Middlebury are marked † in those columns (? where the training data is not stated); to rank models use the official Middlebury and ETH3D test-set leaderboards.

Modes, states and devices

These terms apply to every device:

  • Modes: original = the authors' code with the same checkpoint (fp32 and the authors' own fp16 option, else torch.autocast), portable = fastforks in plain PyTorch, kernels = fastforks with its own kernels (CUDA, or Metal on Apple silicon). Every time column names its dtype or its original precision.
  • Timing: median of warm, synchronised calls after warm-up, one model at a time. Startup (load, first call) is listed separately.
  • Memory is recorded as one of two kinds, never compared with each other: peak torch memory (allocated / reserved, CUDA and ROCm) or the peak process footprint (Apple silicon, where weights and activations share the system memory). A TensorRT engine allocates outside torch: its peak (allocated / reserved) is the engine's device memory plus torch's own peak (allocated / reserved) of the same run.
  • Speed-ups name their baseline (vs original, vs portable, vs fastest portable). When a baseline is missing the cell stays empty; another baseline is not used in its place.
  • States: unsupported = the card does not offer that mode or dtype on this backend, failed = it ran and raised, OOM = out of memory, – = not tested.
  • The reference device is the RTX 5060 Ti below: its rows are the regression floor (tests/test_speed_floor.py). Every other device is a survey with its own page; no floor is kept for it. Adding a device: "Devices" in docs/data/README.md.

Other devices

  • Apple M1 Pro 16 GB (mps): 272 models, 922 rows, measured 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-12.
  • NVIDIA L4 (cuda): 119 models, 238 rows, measured 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08.
  • NVIDIA L40S (cuda): 119 models, 238 rows, measured 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08.
  • NVIDIA A10 (cuda): 119 models, 238 rows, measured 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08.
  • NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (cuda): 117 models, 234 rows, measured 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08.
  • NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (cuda): 174 models, 348 rows, measured 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-08.

Across devices

Each task at its standard input (the overview's). A cell is the fastest validated fastforks mode on that device (portable or kernels, time and dtype), or why there is none; a row needs a survey device measured at that input. Cells compare only rows of the same input and protocol (warm-median: median of warm, synchronised calls after warm-up (at least 5; 2 for calls over 2 s on surveys)); no speed-up is derived across devices, as the modes and dtypes differ. – = not measured at this input.
